newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish-held Cyprus sentences three men for spying.
newsitem.headline: Turkish-held Cyprus sentences three men for spying.

text.p: A military court in the breakaway republic of northern Cyprus has sentenced three men to a total 26 years in jail for spying on behalf of Greek Cypriot intelligence on the divided island.

The three were convicted for collecting military information and taking photographs of military installations in northern Cyprus and passing them on to Greek Cyprus in exchange for cash payments in 1995.
The court passed the judgement on Friday afternoon, sentencing Oner Akkargili to 12 years, Gulbahar Koprucu to eight years and Keskin Ciftcioglu to six years.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974, when Turkish troops occupied the northern third of the island in response to a short-lived Greek Cypriot coup engineered by a junta then ruling Greece.
The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus is only recognised by Turkey.
